notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 20% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Troy Terry is on long-term injured reserve and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Pavel Mintyukov is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Drew Helleson has taken his spot beside Travis Mitchell.
Travis Mitchell was added to the roster on Oct 30 and has played beside Pavel Mintyukov.
Roger McQueen was added to the roster on Oct 30 and has played beside Alex Killorn and Nikita Nesterenko.
Zach Hyman is on injured reserve (neck injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Colton Dach has taken his spot beside Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Kasperi Kapanen.
Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin.
Mattias Ekholm returned in their last game after missing 2 games.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 44% of the team’s power-play time in 13 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 11 games, down from 30% last season.

EDM.head: The Oilers should have the upper hand
EDM.body: Even though Edmonton will be without Hyman, the Oilers have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage. On top of that, Anaheim will be without Terry. The Ducks’ way back in is a power play that gets going.

story.head: Bouchard’s favorite opponent
paras: The Oilers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-2 in Anaheim on Oct 7. The Ducks (5-7-1) lost 7-6 to Buffalo on Oct 29, while the Oil (9-2-2) beat Calgary 4-0 on Oct 28. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Ducks sixth (tied for 26th in the NHL) and the Oilers first (third). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Ducks’ record (.423) is about what their chances are worth. The Oilers’ record (.769) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.622), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Ducks play some of the league’s fastest games (3rd) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (30th). Anaheim has allowed 3.85 goals a game, the second most in the league. As for the Oilers, they lean on their stars more than any team in the league (lowest), have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st) and get their defensemen shooting (3rd). Edmonton has scored 4.23 goals a game, the most in the league. Both teams like to hit, especially the Ducks (4th), so expect plenty of it.

Leo Carlsson (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 13 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Beckett Sennecke (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 13 GP) has a team-high eight goals. Connor McDavid (8 G / 28 A / 36 P in 13 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with 13 points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Anaheim. Leon Draisaitl (12 G / 12 A / 24 P in 13 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, second in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games.
Lukáš Dostál (4-4-1 / .872 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Anaheim, and Tristan Jarry (3-1-2 / .883 SV% in 6 GS) for Edmonton.
At home, Mike Babcock likes to send Podkolzin, McDavid and Draisaitl out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Caulfield, Carlsson and Gauthier.
